title: incident-bot: link on-call diagnostics to runbooks and add auto-runbook suggestions
author: Liam Chen
body:
Motivation:
On-call engineers repeatedly ask for quick links to the most relevant runbooks when the incident-bot surfaces automated diagnostics. Currently engineers must search the runbook registry manually which slows down triage. This PR implements a lightweight linking layer and heuristic-based autosuggest that surfaces the top 3 runbooks for a given diagnostics context and exposes them to the on-call card and incident summary emails.

What changed (single-string description):
- Add a runbook linker module that scores runbooks against diagnostic signatures (error codes, SLO ids, metric anomalies, service tags).
- Expose a /api/runbooks/suggest endpoint guarded by the incident-bot service account.
- Add UI dropdown and quick-link buttons to the OncallCard component in the console.
- Add metadata fields to the runbook registry (tags, affected_services, canonical_errors) and migration script to backfill from legacy YAML.
- Add unit and integration tests for scorer and endpoint; add end-to-end test for UI exposure behind a feature flag.
- Feature-flagged rollout and metrics for suggestion acceptance rate and false-positive rate.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of scorer and API
- [x] Unit tests for scoring heuristics
- [x] Integration tests with runbook registry mock
- [x] UI components behind feature flag
- [x] Documentation and runbook registry migration script
- [x] Telemetry (accept / ignore events)

Testing and rollout:
- Unit: runbook_linker tests cover scoring for 12 canonical cases.
- Integration: incident-bot integration tests with mocked registry pass on CI.
- E2E: Console test added to verify dropdown renders when feature flag enabled.
- Rollout: feature-flag default off; canary to SRE on-call team for 72h, monitor acceptance_rate > 20% and FP < 15% before wider release.

Backward compatibility and security:
- API requires incident-bot service token; no public access.
- No breaking changes to existing runbook API (new endpoint only).
- Migration script is idempotent and guarded by dry-run flag.

Related: ENG-2741 (scoring improvements), SRE-3421 (oncall flow improvements), PM-98 (runbook UX).

review_comments: Ava Patel (2026-02-19): Nicely scoped. Two asks: (1) add a unit test for a merged-error-case where tags are conflicting, and (2) can we log a small shard of the scoring vector for telemetry?
Liam Chen (2026-02-19): Added conflicting-tag unit test and telemetry logging in second commit; logs are sampled at 1% to avoid PII leakage.
Jared Kim (2026-02-20): Left a few nits on logging verbosity and on the migration script - prefer explicit batch sizes and a timeout. Also please add alarm if migration > 24h.
Liam Chen (2026-02-20): Addressed nits: added batch_size config (default 500), migration timeout, and alerting hook. Updated docs to reflect config.
Priya Rao (2026-02-22): Verified integration tests locally and in CI; comments resolved. Approving — small follow-up for QA telemetry thresholds in a later PR.
Ava Patel (2026-02-23): Approved after CI green and e2e canary verification.
